info.title: Python TDD workflow with requirement document parsing

parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

6: Programming.

8: There is also a simplified alias of this type called `Try` that pins
9: the Result type to Exception.
10: """

15: from collections.abc import Callable, Generator, Iterable

43: _TOther = TypeVar("_TOther")
44: _TResult = TypeVar("_TResult")

49: @tagged_union(frozen=True, order=True)

51:     Iterable[_TSourceOut],
52:     PipeMixin,
53:     Generic[_TSourceOut, _TErrorOut],

69:         """Create a new Error result."""
70:         return Result(tag="error", error=error)

72:     def default_value(self, value: _TSource) -> _TSourceOut | _TSource:
73:         """Get with default value.

75:         Gets the value of the result if the result is Ok, otherwise
76:         returns the specified default value.
77:         """
78:         match self:
79:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=ok):
80:                 return ok
81:             case _:
82:                 return value

84:     def default_with(self, getter: Callable[[_TErrorOut], _TSource]) -> _TSource | _TSourceOut:
85:         """Get with default value lazily.

87:         Gets the value of the result if the result is Ok, otherwise
88:         returns the value produced by the getter
89:         """

91:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):
92:                 return value
93:             case Result(error=error):

97:         """Map result.

101:         """
102:         match self:
103:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):

106:                 return Result[_TResult, _TErrorOut].Error(error)

109:         self,
110:         other: Result[_TOther, _TErrorOut],
111:         mapper: Callable[[_TSourceOut, _TOther], _TResult],

113:         """Map result.

115:         Return a result of the value after applying the mapping
116:         function, or Error if the input is Error.
117:         """
118:         match self:
119:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):
120:                 return other.map(lambda value_: mapper(value, value_))

150:         return self.tag == "error"

152:     def is_ok(self) -> bool:

154:         return self.tag == "ok"

156:     def filter(

158:     ) -> Result[_TSourceOut, _TError | _TErrorOut]:
159:         """Filter result.
160: 
161:         Returns the input if the predicate evaluates to true, otherwise
162:         returns the `default`
163:         """
164:         match self:
165:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value) if predicate(value):
166:                 return self
167:             case Result(tag="error"):
168:                 return self
169:             case _:
170:                 return Error(default)
171: 
172:     def filter_with(
173:         self,
174:         predicate: Callable[[_TSourceOut], bool],
175:         default: Callable[[_TSourceOut], _TErrorOut],
176:     ) -> Result[_TSourceOut, _TErrorOut]:
177:         """Filter result.
178: 
179:         Returns the input if the predicate evaluates to true, otherwise
180:         returns the `default` using the value as input
181:         """
182:         match self:
183:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value) if predicate(value):
184:                 return self
185:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):
186:                 return Error(default(value))

188:                 return self

190:     def dict(self) -> builtins.dict[str, _TSourceOut | _TErrorOut | Literal["ok", "error"]]:
191:         """Return a json serializable representation of the result."""
192:         match self:
193:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):
194:                 attr = getattr(value, "model_dump", None) or getattr(value, "dict", None)
195:                 if attr and callable(attr):
196:                     value = cast(_TSourceOut, attr())
197:                 return {"tag": "ok", "ok": value}
198:             case Result(error=error):
199:                 attr = getattr(error, "model_dump", None) or getattr(error, "dict", None)
200:                 if attr and callable(attr):
201:                     error = cast(_TErrorOut, attr())
202:                 return {"tag": "error", "error": error}
203: 
204:     def swap(self) -> Result[_TErrorOut, _TSourceOut]:
205:         """Swaps the value in the result so an Ok becomes an Error and an Error becomes an Ok."""
206:         match self:
207:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):
208:                 return Result(error=value)
209:             case Result(error=error):
210:                 return Result(ok=error)

212:     def or_else(self, other: Result[_TSourceOut, _TErrorOut]) -> Result[_TSourceOut, _TErrorOut]:
213:         """Return the result if it is Ok, otherwise return the other result."""
214:         return self if self.is_ok() else other

216:     def or_else_with(
217:         self, other: Callable[[_TErrorOut], Result[_TSourceOut, _TErrorOut]]
218:     ) -> Result[_TSourceOut, _TErrorOut]:
219:         """Return the result if it is Ok, otherwise return the result of the other function."""
220:         return self if self.is_ok() else other(self.error)

223:         """Merge the ok and error values into a single value.
224:

226:         """
227:         return self.default_with(lambda x: x)

229:     def to_option(self) -> Option[_TSourceOut]:
230:         """Convert result to an option."""
231:         match self:
232:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):
233:                 from expression.core.option import Some

235:                 return Some(value)
236:             case _:
237:                 from expression.core.option import Nothing
238: 
239:                 return Nothing

243:         """Convert option to a result."""

246:     @classmethod
247:     def of_option_with(cls, value: Option[_TSource], error: Callable[[], _TError]) -> Result[_TSource, _TError]:

251:     def __iter__(self) -> Generator[_TSourceOut, _TSourceOut, _TSourceOut]:
252:         match self:
253:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):

264:             case Result(error=error):

268:         match self:
269:             case Result(tag="ok", ok=value):

313:             [
